short: The United States dropped two atomic bombs on the Japanese cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, killing over 100,000 civilians and precipitating Japan's surrender.
full:
On 6 August 1945, the United States Army Air Forces dropped a uranium gun-type bomb, 'Little Boy', on the city of Hiroshima, followed three days later by a plutonium implosion bomb, 'Fat Man', on Nagasaki. The two unprecedented explosions caused catastrophic damage, immediately killing an estimated 70,000 to 135,000 people in Hiroshima and 39,000 to 80,000 in Nagasaki. Tens of thousands more died in the ensuing months from severe burns, radiation sickness, and compounded injuries.

The devastating scale of the destruction, coupled with the Soviet declaration of war on Japan in the intervening days, broke the deadlock within the Japanese Supreme Council for the Direction of the War. Emperor Hirohito announced Japan's unconditional surrender on 15 August 1945, ending the Second World War. The bombings remain the only use of nuclear weapons in armed conflict, sparking enduring ethical and strategic debates over their necessity.
